review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped Mathlib for uses of lower_raise and raise_lower, and for the Multiset.coe_sort and map_coe simp lemmas. The only simp-interface point I found is that lower_raise is not a simp lemma, even though callers pass it to simp by hand. The same pattern appears in Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Finset.lean with lower_raise'. I did not flag raise_lower, because it has a SortedLE hypothesis that simp could not discharge. I also did not flag the `-Multiset.map_coe` removals in the instance proof. They look like a deliberate local workaround for one specific goal shape, and I have no evidence they signal a defect. I could not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed attribute compiles or that it causes no simp-set interactions elsewhere. The finding is low-to-moderate confidence.

findings.excerpt: theorem lower_raise : ∀ l n, lower (raise l n) n = l
findings.problem: `lower` and `raise` are plain recursive defs, and the only way to simplify the composite `lower (raise l n) n` is this lemma. It is an unconditional equation that rewrites to a strictly smaller term, so it is a safe simp lemma, and it terminates. It carries no `@[simp]` attribute. As a result the one downstream use has to pass it by name: the second obligation of `Denumerable.multiset` has `simp [-Multiset.map_coe, List.mergeSort_eq_self _ (raise_sorted _ _).pairwise, lower_raise]`. The sibling file Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Finset.lean has the same situation with `lower_raise'`, which is also passed explicitly.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `lower_raise` as `@[simp]`, and drop the explicit `lower_raise` argument from the simp call at line 97. Leave `raise_lower` without `@[simp]`, since it needs a `SortedLE` side condition that simp cannot discharge. Optionally do the same for `lower_raise'` in Finset.lean.
findings.benefit: Simp then normalizes `lower (raise l n) n` to `l` on its own. Future proofs about the `Denumerable (Multiset α)` encoding no longer need to name the lemma. There is no looping risk because the rewrite strictly simplifies the term.

evidence.excerpt: theorem lower_raise' : ∀ l n, lower' (raise' l n) n = l
